content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a new method for audio and video classification that employs hierarchical representation learning. The method, called multiscale multimodal Transformer (MMT), is composed of a novel multiscale audio Transformer (MAT) and a multiscale video Transformer. Furthermore, the authors propose a set of multimodal supervised contrastive objectives called audio-video contrastive loss (AVC) and intra-modal contrastive loss (IMC) that specifically align the two modalities for robust multimodal representation fusion. MMT outperforms previous state-of-the-art approaches and shows efficiency compared to MBT
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
- The paper proposes an effective method to incorporate audio and video inputs for hierarchical video representation learning
- The proposed method achieves improvement on several video benchmark that requires audio-visual representation.


Weakness 
- The novelty is limited, a slightly different version of MViTv2-B (Li et al. 2022), which can be generalized to audio modality.
- In Table 2 (Ablation study on Kinetics-Sounds, VGGSound), the improvement from AVC+IMC is not so noticeable, so the performance improvement factor seems to be a hierarchical transformer architecture which learns hierarchical representation learning. 
Could you add ablation study on the transformer design? For example, multihead multiscale self-attention (MMSA) in the multiscale transformer.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The proposed method is not well described. The motivation and main contribution in the design is not clear.
No code provided, but they provide hyper parameter settings used for experiment.
content.summary_of_the_review: Although the novelty is limited, The proposed method is simple but effective, and the paper shows good experimental result on action recognition datasets. The model's superiority over other multimodal ViT baselines is unclear, as it is difficult to evaluate based on the reported tables, even very simple conversion of MViTv2-B is not reported. I lean toward rejection now, but I'm looking forward to the author's response.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a multiscale multimodal transformer (MMT) for audio-visual action recognition. The authors propose a novel multiscale audio transformer (MAT) to encode audio spectrums and contrastive losses for audio-visual feature fusion. They achieve good results on three public datasets, i.e., Kinetics-Sounds, Epic-Kitchens-100 and VGGSound.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:

- The motivations of this work are well conveyed. Good literature review.
- The technical description is generally well-organized except for several ambiguities.
- This work achieves good results on three public datasets. It also provides a detailed ablations study.

Weaknesses:

- Figure 1 as well as its caption is not clear to me. 1) The authors claim that “GradCam visualizations in the 6th row indicate that MViTV2 mistakenly consider the text and lyrics” but do not explain how and where it does so. I do not see any supporting details from the visualizations that MViTV treats it as lyrics. 2) I'm not convinced by what the authors conclude that “our MMT can align the sound with the objects”. The highlights are not always on the woodpecker (4th row) or shoes (8th row). 3) In each of the two test cases, these frames look so close that the video appears to be still. Is it essential to show them all?
- The description of the AVBottleneck is unclear. 1) Eq. 5 indicates $E^{AF} = [E^A, \hat{E}^F]$ but figure 2 shows $E^{AF} = [E^F, E^A]$. What is $\hat{E}^F$? Does the position order of each token matter? Please be consistent. 2) The authors claim that “the multimodal bottleneck transformer can be stacked into K blocks”. Does every block contain the initial multimodal tokens? I assume not from the descriptions of this part, but it contradicts Eq. 5.
- There are three transformer modules in the proposed approach. Are they trained iteratively or in an end-to-end manner?
- Figure 5 shows the visualization of another three cases which is similar to figure 1 and has the same flaws. I don’t think it is necessary to repeat visualization if no new point is demonstrated.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: Fair 

Quality: good 

Novelty: good 

Reproducibility: Fair
content.summary_of_the_review: It is good to explore new approaches for multimodal action recognition. The proposed MMT achieves good results. The paper is generally well-written but suffers from several ambiguities. I would be happy to improve my rating if seeing improved figures and technical descriptions.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This work proposes multimodal transformers for multimodal action recognition. In particular they target visual and audio modality. Authors proposes a method that consists of two modality-specific encoders, that are multiscale, and use a fusion method based on AVbottleneck (proposed in a previous work). They also proposed to use two contrastive losses based on class-supervision and intra-modality information. They claim that compared to prior works their loss aligns multimodal representations from the same class instead of same instance. Authors show SOTA performance on three standard audio-visual action recognition datasets with fair improvement. They also show sufficient ablation studies to highlight the importance of the proposed components. This is also augmented with qualitative results showing GRADCAM outputs to compare different models.

Overall the paper is well-written and easy to understand. The idea of multiscale transformers also makes sense for audio. However, it is hard to grasp the key contribution of this work (over prior works) as it seems to be combining different components from prior work and are able to get a model that can beat SOTA.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths
1. Well-written and easy to follow
2. Performance over SOTA is impressive
3. Idea of using label based supervision for intra-modal loss and achieving compact and discriminative features makes sense
4. Algorithm seems better and faster than prior art. Authors have provided information about FLOPS whenever needed
5. Choice of datasets makes sense

Weaknesses
1. As mentioned previously the algorithm seems to be combining ideas from prior work in building a strong model
2. Novelty over prior work was not always clear e.g. in introduction it is not clear what is novel in the proposed multiscale audio transformer over prior work. Is it that multiscale tranformers (from Li et al. 2022) have been used for audio for the first time? Or did the authors proposed a new idea within it to fit this task
3. I understand authors novelty regarding the use of label information in intra-modal contrastive loss but similar ideas have been used in prior works (if not multimodal action recognition)
4. It would have been helpful to provide ablation for individual components such as how does "multiscale" in mutimodal transformers help in performance. What is the effect of lambda in the loss functions.
5. Fig1 was not clear in the print version
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The clarity and quality of the paper is high. However, it is not the case for novelty as mentioned previously. Although the overall model is quite solid as per empirical evaluation, the individual components are not novel. I would not have talked about novelty if the focus of the paper was on something else rather than the model.
content.summary_of_the_review: My ratings are based on the proposed idea being a combination of several prior works. There seems to be some novelty in this work but it is not strong enough or it does not appear so.
